plan.contextChunk: This figure presents three side-by-side ray diagrams, labeled (a), (b), and (c), each showing light meeting a flat horizontal boundary between two media. In every panel a shaded blue rectangle fills the lower half and carries the label n1 at its right edge, the unshaded region above it is labeled n2, and a vertical dashed line marks the normal at the point of incidence. In panel (a) a solid ray annotated Incident ray travels up and to the right inside n1 and splits at the surface: a Refracted ray continues into n2, tilted away from the normal at the marked angle theta_2, while a Reflected ray turns back down into n1 at theta_1, matching the incident angle theta_1 marked on the other side of the normal. Panel (b) shows a steeper incident ray drawn at the angle labeled theta_c, whose refracted ray now runs flat along the interface with a small square and the label theta_2 = 90 degrees, and whose reflected ray leaves at theta_c. In panel (c) the incident ray arrives at theta_1, larger than the dashed reference ray drawn at theta_c beside it, and no refracted ray appears at all, only a reflected ray next to the words Total internal reflection. Read left to right the three panels track one incident angle being steadily increased, which defines the critical angle and the condition under which light is confined entirely to the medium of higher index.

interactionPlan.concept: As the angle of incidence inside a denser medium grows, the refracted ray bends ever farther from the normal until, at the critical angle where sin θ_c = n₂/n₁, it grazes the interface — beyond that angle no light escapes and the boundary reflects it all.
elements: Three side-by-side panels (a), (b), (c) in the default composite view, each an identical boundary diagram at a different incident angle
In each panel: a horizontal boundary line across the middle, with a pale blue shaded rectangle filling the lower half (denser medium)
Italic serif label n₁ inside the shaded lower medium near its right edge of each panel
Italic serif label n₂ in the white upper region near the upper left of each panel
Vertical black dashed normal through the point of incidence at the panel's horizontal center, extending both above and below the boundary
Solid teal incident ray from lower-left to the incidence point, slightly overshooting past the vertex, filled arrowhead placed near the ray tip
Solid teal reflected ray leaving down-and-right at the mirrored angle, arrowhead near its outer tip
Solid teal refracted ray in n₂ bending away from the normal, arrowhead near its outer tip (present in panels a and b only)
Thin angle arcs at the vertex with italic labels θ₁ (incident side), θ₁ (reflected side), θ₂ (refracted side)
Panel (b) only: refracted ray lying flat along the boundary to the right, small right-angle square drawn at the vertex between the normal and the boundary, with the label 'θ₂ = 90°'

Panel (c) only: no refracted ray, thickened/brighter reflected ray, dashed teal reference ray drawn at θ_c with its own arc labeled θ_c, and the two-line text annotation 'Total internal reflection' inside the lower medium
Small italic panel letters (a), (b), (c) beneath or at the upper-left corner of each panel — the dominant per-panel captions, with no competing descriptive subcaption text
Single-panel exploration view: one enlarged copy of the same diagram driven live by the sliders
Optional dashed teal θ_c reference ray with arc label in the exploration view
Collapsible compact readout chip (collapsed by default) that expands to show θ₁, θ₂ (or 'none'), n₂/n₁ and θ_c on separate text lines, plus the relations n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ and sin θ_c = n₂/n₁

interactions.teaches: The textbook's three static panels and the live sweep are the same physics: (a), (b), (c) are just three frozen frames of one continuously increasing incident angle.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: Raising θ₁ swings the refracted ray rapidly toward the surface until it grazes and then vanishes, while the reflected ray always survives and takes up all the light.
interactions.label: Angle of incidence θ₁ (degrees) — single-panel sweep

interactions.teaches: The threshold itself is set only by the index ratio: sin θ_c = n₂/n₁, so a smaller ratio makes total internal reflection begin at a shallower angle.
interactions.label: Index ratio n₂/n₁

interactions.teaches: A persistent dashed θ_c line lets the learner judge at a glance whether the current ray is below or above the escape threshold.
interactions.label: Show dashed θ_c reference ray

interactions.teaches: The numbers behind the picture — θ₁, θ₂, n₂/n₁, θ_c — can be summoned when wanted without cluttering the figure.
interactions.label: Expand numeric readout

demo_steps.title: The figure as printed
demo_steps.narration: Three panels of one boundary between a dense medium n₁ below and a lighter medium n₂ above: in (a) the ray refracts out, in (b) it grazes the surface at θ₂ = 90°, in (c) it is entirely reflected back.

demo_steps.title: Ordinary refraction (a)
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the live single panel at a modest angle: the ray splits, part reflecting at θ₁ and part refracting into n₂ bent away from the normal so θ₂ > θ₁.

demo_steps.title: Bending farther out
demo_steps.narration: Push θ₁ higher and the refracted ray swings toward the surface far faster than θ₁ grows, because n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ with n₁ > n₂.

demo_steps.title: The critical angle (b)
demo_steps.narration: At θ₁ = θ_c ≈ 42° the refracted ray lies flat along the boundary, θ₂ = 90°, and the live ray sits exactly on the dashed reference — this is where sin θ_c = n₂/n₁.

demo_steps.title: Total internal reflection (c)
demo_steps.narration: Beyond θ_c Snell's law has no solution for θ₂ — the refracted ray disappears and all the light returns into n₁.

demo_steps.title: Moving the threshold
demo_steps.narration: Hold θ₁ at 60° and raise n₂/n₁: the dashed θ_c line swings outward and, once θ_c passes 60°, the refracted ray reappears. The indices control the threshold, not the ray.

demo_steps.title: Back to the three snapshots
demo_steps.narration: Returning to the printed figure, (a), (b) and (c) now read as θ₁ < θ_c, θ₁ = θ_c and θ₁ > θ_c — one continuous story frozen at three moments.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Total internal reflection is not a new effect but the point where refraction runs out of room: once θ₂ would have to exceed 90°, Snell's law has no solution and all the light must reflect — and that threshold is fixed entirely by sin θ_c = n₂/n₁.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Default view is the source composite: three equal panels laid left-to-right, separated by generous white space, each labeled only with a small italic (a), (b), (c) — no extra descriptive subcaptions. Each panel has a white upper half (n₂, italic serif, upper left) and a pale blue-tinted lower rectangle with a thin blue top border (n₁, italic serif, lower right). A black vertical dashed normal passes through the incidence point at panel center, extending above and below the boundary. Rays are solid teal (~#1B7A8C), roughly 3px, and should overshoot the incidence point and the shaded block edge slightly as in the source; place filled arrowheads near the outer TIP of each ray, not mid-ray. Panel (a): incident from lower-left, reflected to lower-right, refracted to upper-right at a larger angle, arcs labeled θ₁, θ₁, θ₂. Panel (b): refracted ray flat along the boundary to the right, small right-angle square at the vertex between normal and boundary, label 'θ₂ = 90°' set just above the boundary — reproduce this annotation exactly. Panel (c): refracted ray omitted, reflected ray drawn thicker/brighter, a dashed teal ray at θ_c in the lower-left with arc label θ_c, and the words 'Total internal reflection' on two lines inside the lower medium at the right — reproduce exactly. Single-panel sweep mode enlarges one identical panel, driven by the sliders, with the same styling. The numeric readout is a small collapsed chip in a corner; when expanded, each quantity is its own <text> element on its own line at an explicit x offset (never rely on trailing spaces for spacing), e.g. 'θ₁ = 42°', 'θ₂ = 90°', 'n₂/n₁ = 0.67', 'θ_c = 42.1°', with Snell's law beneath in smaller type.

authoredContext:
Consider what happens when a ray of light strikes the surface between two materials, as shown in the figure(a). Part of the light crosses the boundary and is refracted; the rest is reflected. If, as shown in the figure, the index of refraction for the second medium is less than for the first, the ray bends away from the perpendicular. (Since n1>n2, the angle of refraction is greater than the angle of incidence—that is, θ2>θ1.) Now imagine what happens as the incident angle increases. This causes θ2 to increase also. The largest the angle of refraction θ2 can be is 90°, as shown in part (b). The critical angle θc for a combination of materials is defined to be the incident angle θ1 that produces an angle of refraction of 90°. That is, θc is the incident angle for which θ2=90°. If the incident angle θ1 is greater than the critical angle, as shown in the figure(c), then all of the light is reflected back into medium 1, a condition called total internal reflection. (As the figure shows, the reflected rays obey the law of reflection so that the angle of reflection is equal to the angle of incidence in all three cases.)

Total internal reflection occurs for any incident angle greater than the critical angle θc, and it can only occur when the second medium has an index of refraction less than the first. Note that this equation is written for a light ray that travels in medium 1 and reflects from medium 2, as shown in the figure.

(a) A ray of light crosses a boundary where the index of refraction decreases. That is, n2<n1. The ray bends away from the perpendicular. (b) The critical angle θc is the angle of incidence for which the angle of refraction is 90°. (c) Total internal reflection occurs when the incident angle is greater than the critical angle.

In figure a, an incident ray at an angle theta 1 with a perpendicular line drawn at the point of incidence travels from n 1 to n 2. The incident ray undergoes both refraction and reflection. The angle of refraction o the refracted ray in medium n 2 is theta 2. The angle of reflection of the reflected ray in medium 1 is theta 1. In figure b, the incident angle is theta c which is larger than the angle of incidence in figure a. The angle of refraction theta 2 becomes 90 degrees and the angle of reflection is theta c. In figure c, the angle of incidence theta 1 is greater than theta c, total internal reflection takes place and only reflection takes place. The light ray travels back into medium n 1, with the reflection angle being theta one.

plan.reconstructionNotes: Single wide frame (or three equal panels in comparison mode). Lower half is a pale blue-to-white gradient rectangle with a thin blue border, labeled n₁ in serif italic near its right edge; the white region above is labeled n₂ at upper left. A black vertical dashed normal passes through the incidence point at the horizontal center of each panel. All rays are solid teal (#1B7A8C-ish), about 3px wide, each with a filled arrowhead partway along it indicating propagation direction. Incident ray comes from lower-left going up-right; reflected ray leaves to lower-right at a mirrored angle; refracted ray leaves upper-right at a larger angle from the normal. Thin teal or black arcs near the vertex carry italic labels θ₁, θ₁, θ₂, θ_c. At the critical case, draw the refracted ray flat along the boundary to the right with a small right-angle square at the vertex and the label 'θ₂ = 90°' above it. Above θ_c, omit the refracted ray entirely, fatten/brighten the reflected ray, and place the two-line text 'Total internal reflection' in the lower-right of the shaded medium. The dashed teal θ_c reference ray sits in the lower-left quadrant alongside the incident ray. Curved hand-drawn-style annotation arrows connect the words 'Incident ray', 'Reflected ray', 'Refracted ray' to their rays. Keep a small readout box in a corner listing θ₁, θ₂, n₂/n₁ and θ_c with Snell's law written beneath.

discrepancies: The incident, reflected and dashed θ_c rays extend well BELOW the shaded medium rectangle (they run down to the bottom of the canvas), whereas in the source every ray inside n₁ terminates at the lower edge of the shaded block — the rays appear to float outside the medium they are supposed to travel in.

Panel proportions are distorted: the medium block is an extremely wide, short strip spanning nearly the full 960-unit canvas, while the source panels are roughly 2:1 blocks, so the ray geometry reads much flatter/smaller than in the original.

The 'n₂' label is drawn at ~(102, 85), directly underneath the white readout box placed at (18,14,205×80) — it is completely occluded, so the upper-medium index label is effectively missing in the default view.

The white numeric readout panel (θ₁, θ₂, n₂/n₁, Snell's law equations) is an addition not present in the source and, at 11.5 user units under the ~0.6 viewbox scale, renders at ~7 px — illegible at inline size.
The dashed θ_c reference ray and its θ_c arc are shown in the default (panel-a equivalent) view; in the source the dashed θ_c ray appears only in panel (c).
Label sizes overall (n₁, 'Incident ray', 'Reflected ray', θ₁/θ₂) are noticeably smaller relative to the figure than in the source, where ray labels are prominent.
evaluation.notes: Physics and interaction design are excellent (two sliders, three-panel toggle, six-step narrated demo, correct Snell's-law and θ_c math), but the drawing lets rays escape below the shaded medium, uses an over-wide flat block, and the readout box both occludes the n₂ label and is rendered far too small to read.
action_items: Clamp the incident, reflected and dashed θ_c rays to the shaded medium rectangle (use the rect's y-extent, not y0+h-5, in fClamp's lower bound) so all n₁ rays terminate on the block's lower edge as in the source.
Reduce the panel width (or increase block height) so the medium block has roughly the source's 2:1 aspect and the ray fan occupies a comparable fraction of the frame.

Move the readout box to a corner that is free of artwork (or reposition the n₂ label) so 'n₂' is visible, and increase readout/label font sizes (≥14 user units for annotations, ≥16 for n₁/n₂) so they are legible at inline scale.
Hide the dashed θ_c reference ray by default in the panel-(a) state (or make it visually secondary) so step 0 matches the source's panel (a) exactly, revealing it at the critical-angle/TIR steps.

plan.concept: As the angle of incidence inside a denser medium grows, the refracted ray bends ever farther from the normal until, at the critical angle where sin θ_c = n₂/n₁, it grazes the interface — beyond that angle no light escapes and the boundary reflects it all.
elements: Three side-by-side panels (a), (b), (c) in the default composite view, each an identical boundary diagram at a different incident angle
In each panel: a horizontal boundary line across the middle, with a pale blue shaded rectangle filling the lower half (denser medium)
Italic serif label n₁ inside the shaded lower medium near its right edge of each panel
Italic serif label n₂ in the white upper region near the upper left of each panel
Vertical black dashed normal through the point of incidence at the panel's horizontal center, extending both above and below the boundary
Solid teal incident ray from lower-left to the incidence point, slightly overshooting past the vertex, filled arrowhead placed near the ray tip
Solid teal reflected ray leaving down-and-right at the mirrored angle, arrowhead near its outer tip
Solid teal refracted ray in n₂ bending away from the normal, arrowhead near its outer tip (present in panels a and b only)
Thin angle arcs at the vertex with italic labels θ₁ (incident side), θ₁ (reflected side), θ₂ (refracted side)
Panel (b) only: refracted ray lying flat along the boundary to the right, small right-angle square drawn at the vertex between the normal and the boundary, with the label 'θ₂ = 90°'

Panel (c) only: no refracted ray, thickened/brighter reflected ray, dashed teal reference ray drawn at θ_c with its own arc labeled θ_c, and the two-line text annotation 'Total internal reflection' inside the lower medium
Small italic panel letters (a), (b), (c) beneath or at the upper-left corner of each panel — the dominant per-panel captions, with no competing descriptive subcaption text
Single-panel exploration view: one enlarged copy of the same diagram driven live by the sliders
Optional dashed teal θ_c reference ray with arc label in the exploration view
Collapsible compact readout chip (collapsed by default) that expands to show θ₁, θ₂ (or 'none'), n₂/n₁ and θ_c on separate text lines, plus the relations n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ and sin θ_c = n₂/n₁

interactions.teaches: The textbook's three static panels and the live sweep are the same physics: (a), (b), (c) are just three frozen frames of one continuously increasing incident angle.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: Raising θ₁ swings the refracted ray rapidly toward the surface until it grazes and then vanishes, while the reflected ray always survives and takes up all the light.
interactions.label: Angle of incidence θ₁ (degrees) — single-panel sweep

interactions.teaches: The threshold itself is set only by the index ratio: sin θ_c = n₂/n₁, so a smaller ratio makes total internal reflection begin at a shallower angle.
interactions.label: Index ratio n₂/n₁

interactions.teaches: A persistent dashed θ_c line lets the learner judge at a glance whether the current ray is below or above the escape threshold.
interactions.label: Show dashed θ_c reference ray

interactions.teaches: The numbers behind the picture — θ₁, θ₂, n₂/n₁, θ_c — can be summoned when wanted without cluttering the figure.
interactions.label: Expand numeric readout

demo_steps.title: The figure as printed
demo_steps.narration: Three panels of one boundary between a dense medium n₁ below and a lighter medium n₂ above: in (a) the ray refracts out, in (b) it grazes the surface at θ₂ = 90°, in (c) it is entirely reflected back.

demo_steps.title: Ordinary refraction (a)
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the live single panel at a modest angle: the ray splits, part reflecting at θ₁ and part refracting into n₂ bent away from the normal so θ₂ > θ₁.

demo_steps.title: Bending farther out
demo_steps.narration: Push θ₁ higher and the refracted ray swings toward the surface far faster than θ₁ grows, because n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ with n₁ > n₂.

demo_steps.title: The critical angle (b)
demo_steps.narration: At θ₁ = θ_c ≈ 42° the refracted ray lies flat along the boundary, θ₂ = 90°, and the live ray sits exactly on the dashed reference — this is where sin θ_c = n₂/n₁.

demo_steps.title: Total internal reflection (c)
demo_steps.narration: Beyond θ_c Snell's law has no solution for θ₂ — the refracted ray disappears and all the light returns into n₁.

demo_steps.title: Moving the threshold
demo_steps.narration: Hold θ₁ at 60° and raise n₂/n₁: the dashed θ_c line swings outward and, once θ_c passes 60°, the refracted ray reappears. The indices control the threshold, not the ray.

demo_steps.title: Back to the three snapshots
demo_steps.narration: Returning to the printed figure, (a), (b) and (c) now read as θ₁ < θ_c, θ₁ = θ_c and θ₁ > θ_c — one continuous story frozen at three moments.

plan.keyInsight: Total internal reflection is not a new effect but the point where refraction runs out of room: once θ₂ would have to exceed 90°, Snell's law has no solution and all the light must reflect — and that threshold is fixed entirely by sin θ_c = n₂/n₁.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Default view is the source composite: three equal panels laid left-to-right, separated by generous white space, each labeled only with a small italic (a), (b), (c) — no extra descriptive subcaptions. Each panel has a white upper half (n₂, italic serif, upper left) and a pale blue-tinted lower rectangle with a thin blue top border (n₁, italic serif, lower right). A black vertical dashed normal passes through the incidence point at panel center, extending above and below the boundary. Rays are solid teal (~#1B7A8C), roughly 3px, and should overshoot the incidence point and the shaded block edge slightly as in the source; place filled arrowheads near the outer TIP of each ray, not mid-ray. Panel (a): incident from lower-left, reflected to lower-right, refracted to upper-right at a larger angle, arcs labeled θ₁, θ₁, θ₂. Panel (b): refracted ray flat along the boundary to the right, small right-angle square at the vertex between normal and boundary, label 'θ₂ = 90°' set just above the boundary — reproduce this annotation exactly. Panel (c): refracted ray omitted, reflected ray drawn thicker/brighter, a dashed teal ray at θ_c in the lower-left with arc label θ_c, and the words 'Total internal reflection' on two lines inside the lower medium at the right — reproduce exactly. Single-panel sweep mode enlarges one identical panel, driven by the sliders, with the same styling. The numeric readout is a small collapsed chip in a corner; when expanded, each quantity is its own <text> element on its own line at an explicit x offset (never rely on trailing spaces for spacing), e.g. 'θ₁ = 42°', 'θ₂ = 90°', 'n₂/n₁ = 0.67', 'θ_c = 42.1°', with Snell's law beneath in smaller type.
